messages:
Marta: Heads-up — dedicated-us-west-1 canary for the new multilingual_v2.0 checkpoint was halted by the rollout guard. p99 jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms after the onboard.
Kevin: saw that from CI: perf-ci/latency-smoke failed. Quick glance at logs shows a big increase in kv_cache evictions and a drop in effective batch packing.
CI-bot: perf-ci/latency-smoke FAILED: p99=420ms (baseline=120ms). Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/1717004321.
Liang: can you paste an allocation/profile dump? I want to know which kernel the runtime picked — our kernel-selection heuristic can pick slower generic kernels for larger seq lengths.
Marta: attaching quick profiler snippets below and a token length sample.
```
$ redwood-prof dump --trace 1717004321 --format=text
--- top stacks (samples)
65%  runtime::attention_gpt_qk_kernel_generic
20%  runtime::kv_cache::eviction_hotpath
10%  runtime::batcher::schedule_cycle
5%   other
```
```
Token length histogram (canary): avg=512, p50=480, p90=760
Baseline (previous checkpoint): avg=96, p50=88, p90=160
KV evictions/sec: 120 (canary) vs 8 (baseline)
```
Marta: So two things: avg sequence length increased ~5x, and eviction rate shot up. The batcher started emitting a lot of small batches (few requests per batch) and the runtime switched to the generic attention kernel around seq len > 256, which looks much slower for our mid-size distribution.
Eva: The multilingual tokenizer change we shipped normalizes several scripts and expands some grapheme combinations, which can increase token counts for scripts we didn't test heavily. Could be a tokenizer mapping drift rather than the checkpoint weights.
Samir: Can we bisect the model onboarding commits? Maybe a model config (normalize_unicode, add_special_tokens) changed.
Liang: Also check batching config: we have a threshold batching.max_seq_threshold=256 used to decide kernel selection path and batch packing heuristics. If the new avg is 512, the batcher will reduce packing density and runtime will choose the streaming/generic kernel. Try temporarily raising threshold to 768 on the canary route.
Marta: patched canary route config: `rctl set-config --route /generate --batch.max_seq_threshold 768` and re-ran perf smoke. Result: p99 -> 160ms, kv_evictions/sec -> 18. Still higher than baseline but way better.
Kevin: good signal — kernel selection + batching heuristic explains the latency. Secondary issue is KV key churn: tokenizer produced slightly different token ids for common prefixes so the KV cache hit rate dropped and evictions increased.
Liang: propose next steps:
1) Revert tokenizer config flags in model registry for multilingual_v2.0 (toggle normalize_unicode back) as a short-term mitigation.
2) Add model metadata that overrides batching.max_seq_threshold for this checkpoint during rollout.
3) Add a CI onboarding perf guard: assert average token length delta < 2x and p99 on dedicated-canary <= 200ms.
4) Instrument runtime to emit kernel_selection.heuristic_reason and per-checkpoint token-length histogram to Console.
Eva: I'll open the model registry revert PR and the onboard script change to write token-length histograms into the artifact bundle.
Marta: created canary config patch and holding it so dedicated isn't affected while we revert the model.
Oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created: "Dedicated p99 spike — multilingual_v2.0 onboard" assigned to eng-runtime.
Samir: I'll add the perf guard to CI (perf-ci/latency-smoke) so future onboards fail fast.
Kevin: small ops note: runtime v0.9.3 now logs kernel_selection.heuristic_reason; we should parse that field in perf dashboards and create an alert when heuristic jumps to "sequence_length_threshold" for a checkpoint.
CI-bot: Pull request #412 merged: revert model/multilingual_v2.0 tokenizer config (normalize_unicode=false).
Marta: re-ran canary perf after merge + keeping batch.max_seq_threshold=768: p99=130ms, kv_evictions/sec=6. Canary healthy.
Kevin: root cause summary: tokenizer normalization changed tokenization density -> average seq len increased -> batcher and kernel-selection heuristics produced lower throughput kernel and poorer packing -> higher p99. Secondary: altered token-id patterns reduced KV cache locality, increasing eviction churn.
Liang: follow-ups (owners):
- Eva: model registry revert + PR to onboard scripts (token-length histograms) — ETA 24h
- Marta: keep canary override until next stable onboard — owner for promotion
- Samir: CI perf guard + gating rule — ETA 48h
- Kevin: dashboard alert on kernel_selection heuristic and per-checkpoint token-length drift — ETA 72h
Marta: thanks everyone, keeping the canary pinned and will post when the full rollout resumes. :tada:
Kevin: can we add a tiny unit test in onboard CI that simulates common corpora and asserts token-length multiplier < 2x? saves a lot of triage.
Eva: adding that to the PR now.
Marta: closing thread — resolved for now, will reopen if metrics regress. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
